newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-TRUSTFULL AND CARBONE OPEN ACCOUNTS FOR WEDNESDAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TRUSTFULL AND CARBONE OPEN ACCOUNTS FOR WEDNESDAY.

text.p: Dutchman Orlando Trustfull and Italian Benito Carbone each scored their first goals for Sheffield Wednesday to earn a comfortable 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest on Monday and leave the Midland club anchored to the bottom of the England premier league.
Wednesday dominated the first half without finding the net although it required a fine display of goalkeeping by Forest's Mark Crossley to maintain a clean sheet by the interval.

The home side were soon back on the attack in the second half and lone striker Andy Booth was denied by another superb Crossley block when he raced onto Trustfull's pass through the middle but failed to get enough height on his clipped shot.
But Crossley was powerless to prevent Wednesday deservedly taking the lead after 63 minutes when midfielder Trustfull swept home a low shot from inside the six-yard box .
It was the Dutchman's first goal for Wednesday since he made the 750,000 pounds ($1.3 million) switch from Feyenoord earlier this season.

Trustfull limped off with what looked like a hamstring injury after 80 minutes, but Wednesday pressed forward to seal the game in style with five minutes remaining to lift themselves back into the top 10.

Carbone, a three million pounds ($5 million) buy from Inter Milan, opened his Hillsborough account with an unerring drive from 20 yards after Mark Pembridge had spotted the midfielder's dash forward and slanted back the perfect ball into his path.
